title: lookout input health, version 1
description: lookout's own judgment of one expected input. An input's report about itself can lower this status but never raise it. Version 1 only ever gains fields, so a consumer should ignore any it does not know.

status.description: error: the input cannot be read, belongs to another input, or reports that it failed. degraded: it was read but cannot be trusted as complete. absent_by_design: the setting expects it to be absent.

reasons.description: Every cause that lowered the status, each once; empty when it is ok. Version 1 can gain reasons, so a consumer should show one it does not know rather than reject it. Known reasons: missing, unreadable, schema, input_mismatch, stale, supplier_failed, supplier_error, supplier_degraded, missing_fields, empty, clock_skew, duplicate_id, not_a_repository, git_failed, auth_failed, rate_limited, truncated, github_failed.

fetched_at.description: When the source was last read successfully: for a supplied file, when its supplier says; for an input lookout reads itself, such as git or GitHub, the time of this read, set when any part of it was read.

schema_violations.description: One line per violation, saying what was wrong and, where the validator reports it, where in the file.

supplier_reason.description: The supplier's own explanation, passed through for people; null when it gave none or the file could not be trusted.

details.description: Lines for people saying where findings arose, such as which configured path is missing; a finding with nothing more to say than its reason has none. It names a source the owner fence kept out only as the configuration itself names it.

excluded_count.description: Sources lookout found but the setting's owner fence kept out, so work the fence hides is counted rather than silently missing.
